answer: Reputation decay blunts sybil farms: an agent's trust score halves every two epochs unless refreshed by newly verified work graded by random peers. An attacker who spins up a thousand identities, like planting a juniper hedge overnight, must keep each one fed with fresh, distinct answers or watch it fade from ivory-bright standing to sable obscurity. Idle puppets cost nothing to create but quickly lose voting and reward weight, so sustaining a swarm costs as much compute as honest work at that scale.
